$Comment: The Turkey Graveyard, Harvest Feast's repeatable fight: where the souls of the feast's hunted turkeys
linger, and the Great Turkey with them. Bram the Shepherd opens it from his conversation's graveyard
screen while the feast runs (Dialogues/SeasonsOfOrbis/Harvest_Feast_Shepherd.json). Every area of a copy pastes
Harvest_Feast/Harvest_Feast_Turkey_Graveyard.prefab.json, the Headless Horseman's graveyard with the Great
Turkey's fight's entity, its spawn marker, the points its health packs drop on and a way-out pad in the
entrance room (tools/arena_markers.py writes it), so every fresh paste stages a fresh fight. The prefab's
anchor is the entrance room's floor, so EntryOffset lands an arriving party one block up, standing on it;
the Leave_Instance pad behind them takes a player back out. EntryYaw 180 turns them to face south, into
the graveyard. IntroCamera plays the Horseman's graveyard intro (Hallows_Eve_Graveyard_Intro under
ZiggfreedCommon/CameraSequences), a short sweep over the graves, since both places share one layout.
Season keeps it closed outside Harvest Feast. Share: one party to an area, up to five players, and four
areas to a copy. Complete names the Great Turkey's fight, so the run clears when it falls, and Rewards
rolls Harvest_Feast_Turkey_Graveyard_Clear for each member present as a Claim: full the first clear each
day, half on later ones. InChest puts that Claim in the chest the Great Turkey leaves where it fell,
beside its own two, so no results screen opens: each member sees a banner naming the clear with
ChestKey's line under it. Text names it in the reader's language (harvestfeast.progression.lang), and
its GoalKey is the line each player reads as they arrive: what to do there.
EntryCost is the price of going in: one Wishbone (Martha pays one for each Extra Turkeys handed in),
taken from whoever opens an area for their party; partymates who follow into that fight walk in free.
Confirm is left out, so it is on: before anything is spent, the player opening the area sees
CommonLib's confirm screen with the graveyard's name and description, the Wishbone, how many they hold
and how many it takes, and a button whose words are ConfirmKey's; it spends the Wishbone and sends the
party in, and closing the screen spends nothing. With none, the button is off and the HintKey line says
where Wishbones come from. Change Count to change the price, and Bram's way-in label, which names it,
with it.
